text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on August 17 in history:
1424 - The English defeated the Scots and French at the Battle of Verneuil during the Hundred Years' War.
1585 - Spanish forces, led by Duke of Parma, took Antwerp after a 14-month siege in the Dutch War of Liberation.
1629 - John III Sobieski, King of Poland from 1674 to 1696, born. Polish hero who fought against Swedes, Turks, Tartars and Cossacks.
1743 - The Peace of Abo was signed, ending the Russo-Swedish War of 1741-43.
1786 - Davy Crockett, U.S. frontiersman and politician, born. U.S. congressman 1827-31, 1833-35. Killed by the Mexicans at the Alamo in March 1836.
1786 - Frederick the Great, King of Prussia since 1740, died in Potsdam, and was succeeded by Frederick William II.
1850 - Denmark ceded all forts and property rights on the Gold Coast of Africa to Britain.
1850 - Jose de San Martin, soldier, statesman and national hero of Argentina, died. With Simon Bolivar he led South America's independence movement.
1887 - Charles I, last Emperor of Austria 1916-18, and king of Hungary 1916-19, born.

1893 - Mae West, U.S. sex symbol and actress, born. Her Broadway performance in "Sex" in 1926 earned her an eight-day jail term. The only actress to have an inflatable life jacket named after her, she insisted her birth year was 1893 and not 1892 as is often recorded.
1896 - George Carmack discovered gold in a tributary of the Klondike River, Canada, precipitating the famous gold rush.
1906 - Marcello (Jose) Caetano, Portuguese ruler, born. Prime minister from 1968 until he was ousted in a coup by Antonio Spinola in April 1974.
1929 - Francis Gary Powers, U.S. pilot, born. He was shot down in a spy plane over Soviet territory in 1960, setting off a major diplomatic crisis.
1943 - U.S. forces under Patton relieved Messina, arriving just hours ahead of Montgomery's British Eighth Army, signalling the end of the Sicilian campaign.
1943 - Robert De Niro, U.S. actor and Oscar winner for "The Godfather Part II" and "Raging Bull", born.
1945 - Dr Sukarno claimed independence for Indonesia from the Netherlands by setting up the Provisional Indonesian Republican Government.
1952 - Nelson Piquet, Brazilian grand prix motor racing champion, born.
1960 - Gabon achieved independence from France.

1962 - Peter Fechter, 18, was shot by East German guards as he attempted to flee across the Berlin Wall. Left to bleed to death, his case was the most notorious in the history of the Wall. In July 1996 two former guards were charged with his manslaughter.
1969 - Dr Philip Blaiberg died in South Africa, 19 months and 15 days after receiving a heart transplant, a survival record at the time.
1976 - Severe earthquake shook the Philippine island of Mindanao, leaving about 8,000 people dead.
1978 - Three American balloonists, Ben Abruzzo, Maxie Anderson and Larry Newman, completed the first crossing of the North Atlantic in their balloon, Double Eagle II.
1983 - Ira Gershwin, U.S. lyricist and elder brother of George, died in Beverly Hills aged 86.
1985 - 60 people died and 100 were injured in car-bomb explosion in Christian East Beirut.
1987 - Adolf Hitler's deputy Rudolf Hess was found dead in his cell in Spandau Prison, after hanging himself with an electric cord.
1988 - Pakistan President Zia ul-Haq and the U.S. ambassador to Pakistan Arnold Raphel were killed when Zia's plane exploded after takeoff.
1990 - Former Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere bowed out of mainstream politics when he quit as chairman of the ruling CCM party.
1990 - American singer Pearl Bailey, who entertained two generations with her stage and record performances, died.
1990 - Iraq, dramatically raising the stakes in the Gulf crisis, said it would keep Western civilians at its military bases and other key installations until the danger of war was over.
1994 - Riots spread through Lesotho after King Letsie III dissolved the country's first democratically-elected government for 20 years.
1995 - First reports emerged that Alison Hargreaves, the first woman to climb Everest without oxygen, had been killed by an avalanche on K-2 four days earlier.
1996 - France's first woman in space, Claudie Andre-Deshays, took off from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan for a 16-day scientific mission aboard Russia's orbiting Mir space station.
1996 - Ruth Perry was chosen by a meeting of West African heads of state to chair Liberia's ruling council, thus becoming Africa's first woman head of state.
